title: YAKUZA: The Borrowed Life — Volumes One to Three
author: Mohamed Ansar Kader Meera Sahib
selection: Curated exact excerpts; not the complete manuscript or a blind evaluation.

excerpts.quote: There were thirty-four names.

“We don’t know. Gone. Shipped. On cargo ships out of Yokohama, to God knows where.” Tanabe’s voice cracked, just a little, for the first time since he’d known her. “But that’s not why I came to Tokyo.”
“We think it’s the next shipment.” She put the phone down. “We think there are children in it now. Today. Waiting.”
Fourteen children. Between five and eleven. Huddled together on a pile of dirty blankets. Holding each other. Thin. Filthy. Some with tape still on their wrists.
Fourteen of them were home now.
Twenty were still out there. Somewhere. On the other side of an ocean.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter Seventeen: Six Months of Borrowed Life
excerpts.quote: It was slow. Renji had given him a job of sorts: going through the receipts of the family’s three restaurants, looking for waste. Renji paid him the same as a junior clerk. Not a yen more. Arthur had insisted.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter Seventeen: Six Months of Borrowed Life
excerpts.quote: Renji had stared at the spreadsheet. “How did you *see* that?”

excerpts.chapter: Chapter Seventeen: Six Months of Borrowed Life
excerpts.quote: Arthur wrote the first payment off the debt in his notebook. Forty-two thousand yen.
“Your desk,” said Renji. “Your computer. Your first job.”
“A spreadsheet.”
He had never been paid as *Asa*.
Then, a week later, the same boy. Alone. No friends. No car. Asking for the watch back.
“But the redemption period had ended,” said Arthur.
“No.” Mr Nakamura shook his head slowly. “It hadn’t. It was two days *after* the date. Two days. I’d have given it back to him. Happily.”
It happened sometimes. A word he’d never learnt came easily. His thumb found the right place on a phone without being told.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter Eight: The Weight of Iron
excerpts.quote: His arms shook before the blade reached his shoulders.
Fourteen months of Kanda. Fourteen months of squats and planks and running laps of the garden in the dark. Fourteen months of eating every vegetable Cook Ono could find.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter Four: The House of Asakura
excerpts.quote: “Your stepmother, Sayuri-sama. And your half-sister, Yui. She’s five.”
“Now I know.” His father closed his eyes. “And now I have a six-year-old daughter asleep upstairs.”

“Asakura Asa, Yekaterina Viktorovna. Twenty years old. He is still recovering. He works in an office in Shinjuku. On Thursdays he sweeps the floor of a bar in Meguro. On Tuesdays he eats salmon with his family. His little sister is seven.”
